Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 3a) demonstrates a large, well-defined mass in the right superior mediastinum that exerts significant mass effect, shifting the trachea and mediastinal structures to the left. This presentation of a large, circumscribed mediastinal mass causing contralateral shift is consistent with the suspected diagnosis of primary leiomyosarcoma, distinguishing it from options suggesting left-sided location, ipsilateral shift, or irregular invasive contours.
